DocumentQuestion.description: A question a drafter asks the researcher about one gap in the version it drafted: a README section it could not write, or a data dictionary cell it could not fill. The target is either gap_section, or gap_file, gap_field and gap_column together. question_id is derived from the target, so it is the same in every version that leaves the same gap (docs/specs/drafting.md). A question may offer a suggested_answer, with how it was derived (suggestion_derivation); a suggestion is never placed in the document, and becomes supplied only when a person records it as their answer.

question_id.description: The question's identifier within its document: q- and 16 lower-case hexadecimal digits, derived from the gap it targets.

question_prompt.description: The question, as a short line a person reads before the options.

gap_section.description: The heading of the README section the question would fill, as the drafter wrote it.

gap_file.description: The path of the file whose data dictionary row the question would fill.

gap_field.description: The field whose data dictionary row the question would fill.

gap_column.description: The data dictionary column the question would fill, such as unit.

suggested_answer.description: An answer the drafter suggests, offered to the person with the question and never placed in the document. It becomes supplied only when a person records it, or a correction of it, as their answer.

suggestion_derivation.description: How suggested_answer came about. Present exactly when suggested_answer is.

DocumentQuestion.title: DocumentQuestion

DocumentVersionRef.description: One version of a project document: the document the conductor minted an identifier for, and the version's number within it, counted from 1.

document_id.description: The identifier the conductor minted for the document, a UUIDv7.

version.description: The number of a version within its document, counted from 1.

DocumentVersionRef.title: DocumentVersionRef

GroundingRef.description: The identity and content hash of one retrieved thing a payload rests on. The only way a payload may name an external resource as a decided identity, and the only place it names it: what the reference identifies is read from the evidence item with the same source_id and content_hash (docs/specs/grounding.md). The linter matches every GroundingRef against a retrieval span on both fields.
GroundingRef.title: GroundingRef

description: The payload of an agent that drafts or regenerates a project document: a metadata record, a README, a data dictionary or another document, as text (docs/specs/projects.md). The only payload class that becomes a project document.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

document_title.description: A short name a person can tell documents apart by, such as README for raw/.

media_type.description: The media type of document_text, such as text/markdown or application/json.

conforms_to.description: The schema or profile document_text follows, such as a repository's metadata schema.

document_text.description: The content of the document, as text; a structured record is serialised.

revises.description: The version this document replaces, when an agent regenerates it. Absent for a new document, for which the conductor mints a document_id.

document_questions.description: The questions this version asks the researcher, one for each gap it leaves. A README marks each gap with the HTML comment <!-- dd:gap question_id -->; a data dictionary leaves the cell empty and its source unknown.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).
